chunks.text: Today we will travel to a beautiful city by the Black Sea.
We will talk about Batumi in Georgia.
This is a special place full of nature, history, culture, and friendly people.
Let's go.
Part one.
Where is Batumi?
Batumi is in Georgia, a country between Europe and Asia.
It is in the southwest of Georgia on the coast of the Black Sea.
It is close to the border with Turkey.
Batumi is the second largest city in Georgia after Tbilisi, the capital.
The city has about 170,000 people, but it feels bigger because many tourists visit every year.
Batumi is famous for its Black Sea.
Part two.
The climate.
The weather in Batumi is warm and wet.
It rains a lot, even in summer, but the rain makes the city very green and fresh.
In summer, the temperature is around 25 to 30 degrees Celsius.
People enjoy swimming in the Black Sea.
In winter, it is cool, but not very cold.
Snow is rare in the city, but you can see snow in the nearby mountains.
This mix of sea and mountains makes Batumi very special.
Part three.
A short history.
Batumi is very old.
The first people lived here thousands of years ago.
It was part of the ancient Greek and Roman world.
Later, it became part of the Ottoman Empire for hundreds of years.
In the 19th century, Batumi joined the Russian Empire.
Today, Batumi is part of independent Georgia.
The city is modern, but you can still see history in its streets and buildings.
Part four.
The beach and the boulevard.
One of the most famous places in Batumi is the seaside boulevard.
It is a long park by the sea, about seven kilometers.
You can walk, ride a bike, or just relax by the water.
Along the boulevard, there are palm trees, cafes, fountains, and sculptures.
It is very lively, especially in the evening.
Tourists and locals come here to enjoy the sunset over the Black Sea.
It is a romantic and peaceful place.
Part five.
Landmarks and attractions.
Batumi has many interesting places to see.
Here are some of them.
Alphabet tower.
A tall tower shaped like the DNA helix, decorated with the Georgian alphabet.
Batumi Piazza.
A square with Italian style buildings, cafes, and live music.
Ali and Nino statue.
A moving sculpture of two lovers, symbolizing eternal love between different cultures.
Botanical garden.
One of the largest botanical gardens in the world with thousands of plants from many countries.
Dolphinarium.
A place where people can watch dolphins perform.
Batumi is also famous for its modern architecture with unique skyscrapers and colorful lights at night.
Part six.
Culture and people.
People in Batumi are very friendly and warm.
Most speak Georgian, but some also speak Russian, Turkish, or English.
The culture is a mix of European and Asian traditions.
Georgians love music, dance, and hospitality.
If you visit, they will welcome you with food, drinks, and smiles.
Traditional Georgian dance is very energetic and beautiful.
The costumes are colorful and the movements are strong and fast.
Music is also important.
People love singing folk songs, sometimes in polyphony, with many voices together.
Part seven.
Food in Batumi.
Georgian food is world famous and Batumi is a great place to try it.
Some special dishes are kachapuri, bread filled with cheese sometimes shaped like a boat with an egg on top.
King Kali, dumplings filled with meat, herbs, and spices.
Ajapsandali, a vegetable stew with eggplant, peppers, and tomatoes.
Church Kella, a sweet snack made from nuts and grape juice.
Batumi also has fresh fish from the Black Sea.
People enjoy eating outdoors with wine or mineral water.
Georgian wine is very old and very famous.
It is an important part of Georgian culture.
Part eight, nature and mountains.
Batumi is not only about the sea.
Close to the city, you can find beautiful mountains and forests.
The Ajara Mountains are green and full of waterfalls, rivers, and small villages.
Tourists like hiking, exploring, and visiting old churches there.
One famous place is Matarala National Park.
The name means weeping because it rains so much.
It has amazing nature with rare plants and animals.
This mix of sea, forest, and mountains makes Batumi unique.
Part nine, tourism and nightlife.
Batumi is one of the top tourist destinations in Georgia.
People come from Turkey, Russia, Europe, and even from the Middle East.
In summer, the city is very lively.
There are concerts, festivals, and beach parties.
Batumi is also known for its casinos, which attract many visitors.
The nightlife is bright with music, clubs, and lights.
But Batumi is also good for families with parks, museums, and quiet beaches.
Part 10, daily life in Batumi.
People in Batumi live between tradition and modern life.
Many work in tourism, fishing, or farming.
Others work in hotels, restaurants, or universities.
Life is a little slower than in Belisi.
People enjoy spending time with family and friends.
Hospitality is very important.
If you are a guest, they will always offer you food and tea.
Part 11, why visit Batumi?
So why should you visit Batumi?
Because it has everything.
The black sea and beaches, modern architecture and old history, friendly people and rich culture, delicious food and wine, nature with mountains, forests, and gardens.
Batumi is a city that makes you feel relaxed and happy.
It is colorful, diverse, and full of life.
Outro.
That is all for today's episode of the Slow English podcast.
Now you know many things about Batumi in Georgia.
It is a city by the sea with history, culture, and beauty.
A place where East meets West, and tradition meets modern life.
Thank you for listening to Slow English podcast.
I hope you enjoyed this journey and learned new words in English.
See you in the next episode.
Goodbye for now.
